title: Moses at the Fire, Solomon and the Ant

paragraphs.text: The believers are those who establish prayer, give zakah and are certain about the Hereafter. But for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, Allah has made their own deeds seem pleasing to them, so they wander about blindly. They will have the worst punishment, and in the Hereafter they will be the biggest losers. The Prophet receives the Quran from One who is Wise and Knowing.

Moses once told his family that he had seen a fire, and he hoped to bring back news or a burning torch to warm them. When he reached it, a voice called out, blessing those at the fire and around it, and said, "It is I, Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise." He was told to throw down his staff, and when it moved like a snake, he ran away in fear. Allah told him not to be afraid, because messengers do not fear in His presence. Whoever does wrong and then replaces evil with good will find Him Forgiving and Merciful. Moses put his hand into his garment, and it came out white without any illness. These were among nine signs for Pharaoh and his people. Although they were sure inside that the signs were true, they rejected them out of pride and called them magic.

Allah gave knowledge to David and Solomon, and they praised Him for His favor. Solomon inherited from David and said that they had been taught the language of birds. His army of jinn, men and birds marched in rows. When they reached the valley of the ants, an ant warned the others to enter their homes so that Solomon's soldiers would not crush them unknowingly. Solomon smiled at her words and prayed to be grateful and to do good deeds which please his Lord.
